answer:
Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) works by exploiting client-side vulnerabilities to inject malicious scripts into a user's browser. An attacker can place a script in user-generated content sites, such as bulletin boards or blogs, which is then echoed back to other users' browsers. This allows the attacker to execute scripts in the context of the victim's session, potentially leading to unauthorized actions or data theft [Source 1]. 

To identify potential XSS vulnerabilities, attackers probe entry points and inject common script payloads to test if these points are indeed vulnerable [Source 2].
